wiki_text: In November 2025 Venture Global filed a FERC application (and a corresponding DOE export application) for the Plaquemines LNG brownfield expansion, scaling the project up roughly 40% from its March 2025 announcement. As filed, the expansion comprises 32 modular liquefaction trains built incrementally in three phases, adding more than 30.0 mtpa of peak production capacity and taking the entire Plaquemines complex to more than 58 mtpa peak. Venture Global asked FERC to authorize the increased peak capacity by no later than June 25, 2026. In March 2026 the DOE separately granted a 13% increase (0.45 Bcf/d) in non-FTA export volume, raising Plaquemines' total permitted exports to 3.85 Bcf/d. (GEM models this expansion as the 'Expansion (T37-60)' unit with an inferred baseload of 17.78 mtpa; the 30+ mtpa figure above is peak, not nameplate.)

topic: FERC draft EIS for Stage 5 expansion (April 2026)
wiki_text: On April 6, 2026 FERC issued a draft environmental impact statement for Cheniere's Sabine Pass Stage 5 expansion (Trains 7-9, ~20 mtpa total across two phases), concluding the project's adverse environmental effects could be reduced to less-than-significant levels; the comment period ran to May 26, 2026. Cheniere has finalized a construction agreement with Bechtel and authorized limited early works, targeting a FERC permit in late 2026, construction start in late 2026, a final investment decision in 2027, and first incremental LNG as soon as 2030.
